OUTPUT TO GRADE (note, Hospital):
<output>
Chief Complaint

Syncope

History of Present Illness

Patient is a 71-year-old woman who presented after passing out at home. She reports feeling lightheaded when she stands quickly. On admission, orthostatic vital signs were positive with blood pressure dropping from 132 mmHg to 104 mmHg on standing. Telemetry overnight has been without events. Troponin has been negative on two occasions. An echocardiogram is pending. A CT angiogram of the chest has been ordered to rule out pulmonary embolism.

Past Medical History

Not provided

Medications

Apixaban — active

Allergies

Not provided

Social History

Not provided

Family History

Not provided

Review of Systems

Not documented in today's dictation

Physical Examination

Vital Signs: Blood pressure 132/104 mmHg standing (orthostatic drop noted on admission).

No head injury noted.

Testing Results

Troponin: negative × 2.

A1c: 6.1.

CT angiogram of the chest: ordered.

Assessment

Patient is a 71-year-old woman who presented with syncope and orthostatic hypotension. On examination, she reports lightheadedness with position changes, and orthostatic vital signs are positive with a blood pressure drop from 132 to 104 mmHg on standing. Cardiac etiology has been largely excluded with negative troponin on two measurements and telemetry without events overnight. Pulmonary embolism remains on the differential and is being evaluated with CT angiogram. The clinical picture is most consistent with orthostatic hypotension, likely related to volume depletion or autonomic dysfunction. An echocardiogram is pending to further evaluate cardiac structure and function.

Plan

1. Syncope and orthostatic hypotension — administer 1 liter normal saline bolus and repeat orthostatic vital signs this afternoon to assess response.

2. Rule out pulmonary embolism — continue CT angiogram of the chest as ordered.

3. Cardiac evaluation — echocardiogram pending; continue telemetry monitoring.

4. Anticoagulation — continue apixaban.
</output>

CHECKLIST:
<checklist>
U1: Every clinical fact (diagnosis, finding, value, drug, dose, date, procedure, severity label) can be traced to a dictation, stored panel, or prior note for this patient.
U2: No diagnosis label, subtype, or cause is added that the source does not state (e.g., "CHF exacerbation" stays as dictated, never "HFrEF"). A label never contradicts its own number ("Na 146" is never "hyponatremia").
U3: Every number matches the source exactly.
U4: No unit is guessed on an ambiguous value (drip rate, lab, threshold). Celsius stays Celsius. A bare weight is never turned into pounds. An oral dose may gain "mg" ("furosemide 40" to "40 mg" is fine).
U5: Every medication's status matches the tracker. A held drug reads held. Nothing is restarted, started, or stopped that the tracker does not show.
U6: A fact from an earlier day appears only with its date ("Cr 1.1 on Oct 1"), never as today's.
U7: Something planned is never written as done ("ablation scheduled" never becomes "s/p ablation").
U8: No placeholders: {ADDRESS}, {PHONE}, [Today's date], [Physician name].
U9: No narration about documentation ("dose not specified in dictation"), and no "No past medical history documented" when PMH simply was not dictated.
N1: Every clinically meaningful dictated statement appears somewhere in the note: numbers, named terms (POLST, drug names), instructions.
N2: A physician's hedge survives ("possible early pneumonia" stays visible even if confirmed later in the same dictation).
N3: No exam was dictated: the exam section says not examined or not documented. No normal exam is invented, and no "denies..." statements are invented.
N4: A bedside check stays a reminder ("check for dysuria" never becomes "reports dysuria").
N5: A drug already given is written as done, not re-ordered in the Plan ("restarted metoprolol this morning" is not a plan item).
N6: A section with nothing dictated is empty and labeled as such (see Flag 2 on the exact wording). N6 accepts either wording: 'Not dictated' or 'Not provided'.
</checklist>

- Do not grade style, tone, or length. Only the checklist items.
